core: JavaScript bindings declared with let and const
supporting: the temporal dead zone as a practical ordering rule

claims.claim: A JavaScript lexical declaration uses let or const to create bindings in a lexical environment.
A let binding can be assigned a different value after its declaration.
A const declaration must include an initializer and a const binding cannot be reassigned after it is initialized.
Let and const declarations are block-scoped, so a binding declared inside a block is not available outside that block.
A nested block may declare a new binding with the same name; inside that block the inner binding is the one named by the identifier.
Accessing a let or const binding before its declaration is evaluated produces a ReferenceError because it is in the temporal dead zone.
